frequency_question: How often do disciplined legislative majorities with unified intent successfully pass their core restrictive voter/administrative eligibility bills through the chamber they control within a standard two-year legislative window?
membership_rule: Includes major legislative efforts by a congressional majority chamber to pass national proof-of-identity or eligibility verification laws between 2011 and 2026. Excludes minor technical amendments, bipartisan consensus bills, or non-binding resolutions.

cases.name: Securing America's Future Economy Act attempts / SAVE Act initiatives (House passage phase)
REINS Act / Regulatory Accountability major package pushes
HR 1 / For the People Act (Democratic majority house passage)
American Health Care Act (House passage phase)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named instances representing primary partisan vehicle votes in a controlled chamber; baseline reflects 100% passage rate when a disciplined majority leadership forces a priority vote within its own chamber.
known_gaps: Focuses strictly on the originating chamber where the principals' direct will and capability are tested, setting aside bicameral friction per the forbidden rules.
skeleton: 4 major partisan legislative control pushes evaluated for intra-chamber passage capability under unified caucus intent.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 4 documented major partisan vehicle attempts meeting the intent-and-capability threshold.
validity_reason: Valid through the duration of the current congressional seating arrangement; expires upon the swearing-in of a new Congress where internal caucus dynamics could shift.
